asr_text: This news feels like a short play in three acts. Act one was 20 percent. Act two brought an unexpected turn. Act three was an unexpected move in oil prices. The curtain rose on July 13. At 10:16 a.m., Trump posted that the United States would seek a 20 percent charge on all cargo passing through the Strait of Hormuz. The aim was to recover the cost of U.S. efforts to keep the strait safe. But 20 percent was not a finished system. The post did not say who would pay, how the money would be collected, or what legal basis would support it. For the moment, only a large number stood at center stage. The number stayed at center stage for about a day. Then the story took a sharp turn.
